eips.title: In-mempool signature and proof aggregation
eips.summary: Testnet v03 on Daisugi runs a simple version of it, and it is the reason the design has no SPHINCS verification precompile.

moments.context: Antonio noted they launched testnet v03 on Daisugi with a simple version of EIP-8288, demonstrating one transaction containing a STARK proof of 20 transaction signatures using SPHINCS.

Answering Daniel Cason's request for a SPHINCS+ verification precompile, Antonio explained that individual signatures are not verified once a transaction is in a block — they are aggregated, and what gets verified is the zero-knowledge proof of the aggregation, so no precompile is planned.

eips.title: Frame Transaction
eips.summary: Raised from the floor and in chat as a way to bundle transactions and so cut how many signatures a high-volume signer burns per day.

moments.context: Matteo Vicari argued that pairing post-quantum signatures with account abstraction — frame transactions among them — lets a high-volume signer like Circle bundle transactions, which shifts the per-day signature count that drives the lifetime debate. pbark had made the same point in chat a few seconds earlier: "couldn't you bulk transactions together? (with frames)".
Matteo Vena called it a very valid point, saying frame transactions should give an immense benefit and save a large part of the signature budget.
